newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian bank shares fall, investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian bank shares fall, investors sidelined.

text.p: Shares on the Amman stock exchange fell 0.37 percent on Tuesday in quiet trade as leading bank stock slipped and institutional investors steered clear of the market, brokers said.
They said many investors were waiting for 1996 results to be announced for a number of blue-chip firms before committing themselves.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.58 points to 155.76 points in turnover of 449,000 dinars ($634,000).
"This week demand has been lower, even from the foreign investors," said one broker. Traders have said international funds had been buying selectively on the Amman bourse in recent weeks.
Arab Bank fell 1.25 dinars to 267.00 dinars in trade worth 80,000 dinars, making it the most heavily traded share on Tuesday.
Bank of Jordan, which fell 0.16 dinars to 3.00 dinars and Jordan Investment and Finance Bank, which shed 0.05 dinars to 3.20 dinars, joined the downward trend.

Just two shares rose on Tuesday, the barely traded Jordan French Insurance which rose 0.03 to 1.91 dinars and the recently merged Jordan National Bank, which rose a modest 0.01 dinars to 1.94 dinars, recouping some of last week's losses.
Another 19 shares fell and 18 traded without changing.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.30 percent to 81.71 points.
